context:
Fig. 1.7, Demographic Transition Theory, is a graph with Time along the X-axis and 'Birth and death rates (per 1000 people)' from 0 to 40 along the Y-axis. It is divided into five vertical bands labelled 1 High stationary, 2 Early expanding, 3 Late expanding, 4 Low stationary and 5 Declining.

A blue line labelled 'Birth rate' and a black line labelled 'Death rate' both start near 38 to 40 in stage 1 and run close together. In stage 2 the black death-rate line falls steeply while the blue birth-rate line stays high. In stage 3 the blue birth-rate line falls steeply while the black line continues to fall more gently. In stage 4 both lines are low and almost together, near 10. In stage 5 they are shown as broken lines, with the blue birth-rate line dipping below the black death-rate line.

A green shaded area between the two lines, spanning stages 2, 3 and 4, is labelled 'Natural increase'. A blue shaded area between the two lines in stage 5 is labelled 'Natural decrease'. An orange area rising across the whole graph is labelled 'Total population'.
